How to Hang a Bathroom Painting Set of 3

1. Measure your wall first: Use a tape measure to find the total width of the wall or the section you want to fill. Aim for the combined width of all three prints to cover around two-thirds of that space — this keeps things balanced and avoids the prints looking too small or too cramped.

2. Mark the centre point: Find the centre of your wall section and use a pencil to mark it lightly. Hang the middle print centred on this mark, then work outwards to position the left and right prints with an equal gap between each one — 5 to 8 cm is a good starting point.

How to Hang a Set of 3 Flowers Artwork Prints in a Bathroom

1. Measure your wall space: Decide how much horizontal wall space you have available, then divide by three to work out the ideal width for each individual print. Allow a gap of around 3–5 cm between each print so the set feels connected but not cramped.

2. Find your hanging height: Aim to centre the prints at roughly eye level — about 145–150 cm from the floor to the middle of each print works well in most bathrooms. If you're hanging above a bath or basin, measure up from the top of the fixture rather than the floor.

3. Mark your positions lightly in pencil: Use a spirit level to make sure all three prints will sit perfectly straight and at the same height. Mark the top centre of each print's position on the wall before you put in any fixings.

4. Hang and step back: Fix your prints, step back, and check the spacing looks even from a distance — adjust if needed. For a bathroom, choose the wrapped canvas option as it handles moisture far better than paper prints.

Best for: bathrooms, kitchens and any damp or high-humidity rooms where a paper print might not hold up as well over time.
